items.title: Our church has a $1.5 million bequest earning 3.75% in a savings account. Are we throwing money away?
items.content: “Given the size and long-term nature of this gift, we want to make sure the funds are managed prudently.”

items.title: In a wild October for markets, these stocks were the biggest winners and losers
items.content: Many Big Tech stocks were hit hard but the S&P 500 showed strength under the surface, with a majority of stocks showing gains for the month.

items.title: We stopped helping our neighbors with free home repairs and our friendship cooled. Who’s to blame?
items.content: “Last summer, they complained about needing to replace their roof. A few months later, they bought a new SUV.”

items.title: Data centers are a political third rail. West Virginia is grabbing it anyway.
items.content: West Virginia wants more data centers, even as other states slam the brakes on them.

items.title: Reddit shares on track for biggest-ever one-day drop. It’s not the last of the bad news, analysts say.
items.content: Shares in the online discussion platform tumbled 25% on Friday morning after the company issued a lower-than-expected revenue outlook.

items.title: This strategist correctly recommended shorting Big Tech debt last year. Now he says the yields make it attractive.
items.content: Yields ranging from 6% to 8% on tech bonds provide more competition against stocks than before.

items.title: It’s the strangest job market the U.S. has ever seen. The low-hire, low-fire economy turns 3 years old.
items.content: America has always been a job-creating machine. It has broken down for three straight years, and the implications could be with us for a long time.

items.title: AMD’s stock slides after Intel earnings reveal two big issues
items.content: Intel is struggling to make enough AI server chips and dealing with a weak PC market. Investors will soon find out the degree to which AMD may be suffering from the same problems.

items.title: This one chart tells you everything you need to know about Exxon, Chevron and BP’s forecast-beating earnings
items.content: One slide in ExxonMobil’s investor presentation after its third-quarter earnings explains the financial situation for the integrated oil giants very neatly.

items.title: ‘He was heartbroken’: My husband’s kids abandoned him when he was dying. Was he right to leave everything to me?
items.content: “In the end, he left them a few sentimental mementos, some collectibles and old photographs.”
